findings.premise: Calling current() before checking existence and expectedRevision permits not-found/conflict rejection before reading secrets.

findings.premise: Returning a timeout reply while preparation/reaping continues preserves maintenance exclusion until the actual operation finishes.
findings.evidence: LLD §2.2 permits timeout/canceled results at ten seconds while a reaper retains capacity; §6 likewise settles timeout while preparation remains pending. But §3.5 releases the unary maintenance hold on the internal reply. Existing holdingForward explicitly resolves its hold when 'envelope.kind === reply', and Router also ends request activity on that reply. Keeping a supervisor capacity slot does not retain either hold or activity. The design specifies no separate lifetime mechanism for work continuing after the response. summary.prose: Run each connection test in a disposable child process, using the same effective draft and credential rules as Save. The daemon enforces a ten-second deadline, cancels obsolete requests and returns only a safe reachability result after worker cleanup. This story supplies the backend contract; form layout and client stale-result handling remain S005.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a daemon-owned application service over the existing repository JSON registry and driver implementations. Separate saved commit, runtime activation and client refresh; use immutable credential generations and atomic JSON replacement rather than pretending the filesystem and keychain share a transaction. Temporary configurations remain in daemon memory under a workbench lease. All descriptions below are proposed architecture, not assertions of current implementation.

consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: type ConnectionScope = 'saved' | 'temporary'; interface ConnectionKey { repoRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; id: string } interface SafeConnection { key: ConnectionKey; revision: string; kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; label?: string | undefined; publicConfig: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; declaredFamily?: string | undefined; registeredFamily?: string | undefined; effectiveFamily: string; compatibilityWarning?: string | undefined; credentialPresence: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>> } type CredentialPatch = { action: 'keep' } | { action: 'replace'; value: string } | { action: 'clear' }; interface DriverDescriptor { kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; publicInputSchema: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; secretSlots: readonly string[] } interface ManagementCapabilities { version: 2; daemonEpoch: string; features: readonly string[]; receiptRetentionDays: 30 }

consumedContracts.name: Revision-checked mutation and recovery outcomes
consumedContracts.purpose: Make persistence and retries truthful across registry and credential boundaries.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface OperationTicket { operationId: string; lookupRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; connectionId: string; mode: "create"|"update"|"remove"; issuedAt: string; expiresAt: string; signature: string } interface OperationStatusRequest { ticket: OperationTicket } interface MutationRequest { ticket: OperationTicket; operationId: string; key: ConnectionKey; mode: 'create'|'update'|'remove'; expectedRevision?: string | undefined; publicPatch?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined; credentials?: Readonly<Record<string, CredentialPatch>> | undefined } type ManagementErrorCode = 'invalid-input'|'duplicate-id'|'conflict'|'not-found'|'busy'|'registry-unreadable'|'secret-unavailable'|'recovery-required'|'session-expired'|'upgrade-required'|'operation-mismatch'|'reconciliation-required'; interface CommittedOutcome { operationId: string; revision: string; registration: 'persisted'|'session-added'|'removed'; activation: 'active'|'pending'|'failed'|'not-applicable'; credentialCleanup: 'complete'|'pending' } type MutationOutcome = { status: 'committed'; value: CommittedOutcome } | { status: 'rejected'; code: ManagementErrorCode; message: string }; type OperationStatus = { status:'committed'; value:CommittedOutcome } | { status:'pending'|'not-seen'|'reconciliation-required' }; interface ActivationRetry { key: ConnectionKey; committedRevision: string }

boundary.internal: Transient process probe transport, deadline/cancellation and sanitization. Uses foundational context slots without depending on s3’s session implementation.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Safe saved-config read/patch, canonical repo validation, driver profiles, registry metadata/receipts and crash recovery, immutable secret generation staging, compatibility adapters and lease accounting foundation. Does not own temporary storage or rich manager layout. Preserve saved-only scope-local lookup and legacy pinned-family values; signed operation tickets make expiry/replay decidable after receipt pruning. Own the shared memory-only conversion/probe driver foundation, converter-cache policy/identity changes and private DuckDB lifecycle (sc8), completed before the S002/S003 branches.

Session open/resume/heartbeat/end, memory-only temporary overlays and receipts, trusted execution-context propagation through analyzer/tool/MCP call paths, expiry and saved/temporary collision rules. Bind the S001-owned sc8 file execution policy to session identity and expiry; S001 owns conversion, cache-policy isolation and private DuckDB lifecycle. Every native/converted kind uses that foundation rather than a branch-local converter.
Removal coordination for both scopes, busy/revision enforcement, confirmation state, postcommit credential cleanup retry and operation-status recovery. Never invokes source data deletion.

Settings contributions and shared command routing, themed editor/forms, filters, dirty guards, stale-test suppression and truthful feedback in extension and external IDE. HLD has inspected the external pane, actions, service, mirrored types and Settings registrations; S005 implements the recorded plan and validates its mirrored contract before integration acceptance.

nonFunctional.performance: Draft tests have a 10-second parent-enforced deadline, with forced child reap if graceful termination fails. Workbench heartbeat is 30 seconds and expiry 90 seconds after last valid heartbeat. Mutations serialize per repo; list/filter work does not perform driver probes. LLD load tests must verify no leaked children, leases or session entries after cancellation/expiry.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns every saved/temporary config and credential decision; client labels/PIDs are not authorization. Registered-root eligibility gates management and temporary operations; saved-only analysis preserves canonical scope-local lookup without gaining mutation rights. Safe read responses return a profile allowlist and presence booleans only. Secrets, capabilities and full requests never enter logs, receipts, prompts, artifacts, telemetry or checkpoints. Temporary inputs never reach disk or keychain. A test worker receives config via private IPC and may not emit raw driver errors. Temporary file conversion, query spill and metadata/logging are part of the no-persistence boundary, including test workers.
nonFunctional.observability: Use getLogger with operation ID, safe code, repo ID, scope, revision and phase only; timing and counters for commit, activation, recovery, timeout, busy refusal and session expiry. No raw exceptions or endpoint/options. Operation status exposes committed truth even when response delivery or activation failed. Recovery-required and cleanup-pending are visible and actionable.
nonFunctional.durability: Saved JSON remains authoritative. Same-directory atomic rename/fsync commits registry, revisions and receipts together; immutable keychain generations preserve previous effective credentials until commit. Recover preparation records before enabling mutation. Issue signed 30-day operation tickets; preserve receipts through ticket expiry and pending cleanup, and distinguish expired-unreceipted from valid-not-seen after restart. Temporary state and receipts expire on explicit session end, 90-second lease loss or daemon epoch change.

One parent operation owns zero or one child; no reusable workers. Global limit4, one outstanding per transport; keep capacity until actual child close. Drop request records/timers/listeners and plaintext references after exit.

At deadline/cancel send cancel over private IPC, allow250ms graceful cleanup then SIGKILL owned child and await close; result timeout/canceled may return at10s while capped reaper owns capacity until close. A stuck reap cannot enable unbounded retries.
Normal success withheld until child disposes driver/resource and exits. Failed/hung close leads timeout, not reachable.

dataModelChanges.details: Implement sc4 in shared types/wire validators. Extend method catalog by test/cancelTest and classify both main-daemon routes. Result identity is correlation, not authority; immutable snapshot is request-local memory, never persisted.

Daemon transport identity -> 0..1 pending operation; operation ->0..1 owned child, plus bounded reaping state. operation owns timer, IPC nonce, abort cleanup and ephemeral effective config. Child ->exactly1 disposable driver ->0..1 private file resource. No parent pool registration. Future S003 only supplies readonly snapshot callback. Proposed new supervisor src/daemon/db/draft-test.ts and isolated entry src/bin/insrc-connection-test.ts; private messages validate config and return fixed codes only. Fork inherits no credentials or INSRC logging configuration: minimal platform/runtime environment, ignored stdio and silent worker logger initialized before driver imports; no argv/env config, runfiles, shell, keychain/registry/graph imports or IPC daemon access. Worker uses imported factory and sc8 memory-only policy. Source/compiled entry resolution tested; startup crash and broken IPC safely fail. File factories disable persistent DuckDB install/cache/spill per sc8. Construction alone is insufficient. Await the explicit registered-kind probeReachability operation described below; never return schema completeness. DynamoDB is an explicit exception to config-only IPC: parent-prepared runtimeAuth travels only in private worker start message as detailed below; worker still inherits no credential environment.

Factory construction NEVER implies reachable. Add S002-only DraftProbe interface { probeReachability(): Promise<void>; close(): Promise<void> } in proposed src/daemon/db/draft-probe.ts. Concrete driver classes implement this extra internal method without changing shared BaseDriver, registry factory signatures or sc1/sc8. Worker uses exact registered-kind allowlist and checks method presence; absence fails unsupported, never reachable. Driver probes: postgres/cockroachdb SELECT 1 through pg; mysql/mariadb pooled SELECT 1; sqlite read-only open then SELECT 1 (missing file must not be created); mssql SELECT 1; oracle SELECT 1 FROM DUAL; clickhouse SELECT 1; redis/valkey/keydb explicitly connect lazy client then PING; mongodb admin ping; cassandra client connect then SELECT release_version FROM system.local; nats connected flush; dynamodb authenticated ListTables Limit1 without exposing names; etcd authenticated bounded range limit1; memcached version. No writes or schema enumeration. File kinds csv/tsv/json/jsonl/ndjson/parquet/arrow/feather/avro/bson/fixed-width/xlsx explicitly call private readerPath under memory-only policy and issue a bounded SELECT on the selected local target; parse/load errors fail; empty valid input can succeed; xlsx must select real sheet, not fake fallback. No completeness claim. Add methods at src/daemon/db/drivers/pg.ts, mysql.ts, sqlite.ts, mssql.ts, oracle.ts, clickhouse.ts, redis.ts, mongodb.ts, cassandra.ts, nats.ts, dynamodb.ts, etcd.ts, memcached.ts, duckdb-file.ts (each name resolved under src/daemon/db/drivers/). Add exact29-kind coverage assertion, actual unreachable/bad-auth/malformed-file negatives and lazy factory success/probe failure tests. S002 owns these test-specific operations; no sc8 converter redesign.

src/shared/logger.ts must remove top-level mkdirSync and defer mkdir/config reads/transports to non-worker logger creation. Add explicit internal probe-worker mode selected via fixed nonsecret bootstrap environment before first module import; worker fork overwrites INSRC_MODE to probe-worker, filters all inherited logger/Node injection variables, and uses dynamic driver imports only after selecting mode. In probe-worker getRoot returns disabled pino with in-memory no-op destination; it must never call resolveLevel/read config, mkdir, pino transport, pino-roll or stdout/stderr sink. Guard top-level path imports for side effects. Existing daemon/cli/mcp modes preserve current lazy creation and transport behavior. Verify fresh compiled and tsx processes, isolated HOME/TMP and actual PATHS.logDir, spies on fs mkdir/read config and recursive filesystem watches plus path/password canaries on startup/init/error/close; ignoring stdio alone is not evidence.

Add readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined to server-created TrustedRpcContext in src/daemon/request-context.ts. src/daemon/server.ts directDispatch creates per-unary-request AbortController and passes the signal with trusted identity/epoch; returns abort callback. IMPORTANT: cancellation MUST NOT suppress internal completion delivery. After unary handler settles directDispatch emits exactly one internal reply (fixed failure projection when needed), even if signal aborted; IpcServer alone discards socket delivery on closed/canceled request using its existing settled/socket guard. This supersedes the earlier instruction to suppress directDispatch delivery. Thus wrappers can observe handler completion after disconnect. src/daemon/threads/maintenance-entry.ts holdingForward keeps the unary maintenance hold until internal reply (not cancel), uses idempotent release, drops only external delivery after cancellation, and handles cancel-before-admission without starting handler. src/daemon/threads/router.ts uses once-only ended callback for unary reply/error, not unary cancel; preserves internal completion delivery to maintenance wrapper while suppressing client writes at outer server. Keep existing stream cancellation behavior unchanged and once-only. Pending routed unary handlers not owned by this story retain current completion semantics; test/cancel/legacy methods are classified main-daemon in src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts. src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts forwards trusted context to optional second testConnectionRpc parameter and v2 supervisor, never serializes AbortSignal into worker threads. A handler ignoring optional signal still emits completion and cannot strand holds/activity. src/daemon/index.ts stops supervisor admission and drains owned child/preparation work during shutdown; child grace250ms then SIGKILL only owned PIDs. Tests use real IPC disconnect with maintenance locking and router onRequest activity enabled: cancel during preparation/init/close, completion after disconnect, error, unknown method, and pre-admission cancel must return counters/holds exactly once to baseline; no socket late reply and no early maintenance admission while actual handler work is running. Supervisor response terminal state and reaper capacity remain distinct; parent-owned cleanup continues tracked after timeout, without suppressing internal reply or leaking request bookkeeping. Completion/hold release here is subject to the separate RequestLifetime drain protocol below: an internal reply alone MUST NOT release maintenance or activity when registered work remains.

Add SavedConnectionManagement.prepareDraft(context: ManagementRequestContext, request: Pick<DraftTestRequest, 'key' | 'expectedRevision' | 'publicPatch' | 'credentials'>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<EffectiveDraft> in src/daemon/db/management.ts. Under existing per-root serialized gate validate context/root, metadata-only owner/registration/recovery state through probeMetadataReady() (NOT current() or enabled()), snapshot config and revision, infer create/update, enforce existence/expectedRevision, then call shared materializeDraft with readonly owned reference reader. Never list(), apply(), pool.reload(), mutate(), stage/activate, tickets or receipts. Owner-aware reader only accepts refs enumerated from selected snapshot after revision checks; create cannot resolve arbitrary supplied refs. Hold gate through readonly credential materialization so concurrent mutation/cleanup cannot delete Keep generation while it is read; release immediately after immutable plaintext snapshot built, not for network test. Check signal after every await and before returns; hanging preparation retains bounded supervisor slot and queued aborted gate callback must not read secrets/spawn when eventually admitted. No late spawn after deadline. No raw snapshot returned to client or child beyond effective config. Tests snapshot exact registry/keychain and spy zero pool reload/staging/writers; concurrent saved update/delete cannot race Keep acquisition. Future temporary resolver uses equivalent readonly owner contract, no S003 store implementation. After shared materializeDraft, call prepareRuntimeConfig before handing config to worker; S002 supervisor resolves Dynamo runtime identity separately via readonly daemon helper, never persisted in effective config.

dataModelChanges.entity: Runtime path preparation shared with activation
dataModelChanges.details: Extract resolveConfigPath and resolveAndCheckRepoPath from src/daemon/db/pool.ts into proposed src/daemon/db/runtime-config.ts as side-effect-free exported prepareRuntimeConfig(config: ConnectionConfig, canonicalRoot: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ConnectionConfig>. Both pool activation and S002 prepareDraft/legacy preparation call it after materializeDraft and before factory/IPC. Select path policy by registered kind/familyOf(kind), never pinned family. Preserve existing lexical repo-root containment and readable-path checks and schemaSource.path resolution; never cwd-relative resolution. File paths become absolute. Normalize SQLite effective path using existing path-over-url precedence from sqlite.ts: accept path, plain URL path or decoded local file URL, reject remote file URL authorities and non-file schemes; resolve relative path against canonical root, check containment/readability, put result in config.path so factory opens that exact readonly path. dataModelChanges.entity: Metadata-only draft admission before credential readiness
dataModelChanges.details: This supersedes prepareDraft's earlier instruction to call current() first. At startup full enabled validation remains unchanged before service installation. prepareDraft under per-root gate validates trusted context, obtains probeMetadataReady snapshot, parses/enforces registry envelope metadata with the shared metadata validator extracted from current() without calling enabled, and selects requested ID/revision. If missing/stale/duplicate return existing sanitized code before ANY keychain call. After admission, recheck abort, validate signing authority availability if required, selected profile and generation ownership, then materialize only selected config with owned-reference reader. Never scan unrelated connection credentials in this probe-only path. Failure in metadata fence returns recovery-required/upgrade-required before secrets; missing signing key after valid admission still fails. Immutable selected snapshot held under same root gate through readonly selected credential read, runtime paths and completion; no mutation, no generation cleanup. This is an internal adapter implementing consumed sc1/sc2/sc3, not a change to public wire or weakened mutation readiness. Test through openManagedRoot's actual production callback with injected fake keystore, not always-true service fixture: reset keychain counters AFTER startup, then missing/stale/duplicate draft must issue zero getKey calls (including signing keys), zero stages/writes/spawn, while valid target reads only signing key plus selected owned credentials, never unrelated credential canary; missing key and registry/owner drift remain refused. dataModelChanges.entity: Separate unary response and operation-drain lifetimes
dataModelChanges.details: Introduce internal RequestLifetime in src/daemon/request-context.ts, created server-side in src/daemon/server.ts BEFORE forwarding unary request. API registerDrain(work:Promise<void>):void, seal():void, drained:Promise<void>; registerDrain accepts only before seal, uses all-settled work completion, never settles drained until sealed AND every registered work item settled. Expose only registerDrain on TrustedRpcContext, lifetime owned by internal RequestEnvelope; none is deserialized from client params or serialized to worker-thread wire. draft-test supervisor synchronously registers its whole operation-drain promise before first await; drain encompasses root-gate queue, pending root/keychain/AWS preparation, asynchronous spawn, child close/reap, and all cleanup/listener/timer releases, including work continuing after timeout result. Terminal response promise settles at deadline independently. directDispatch seals request lifetime in its unary handler finally and still delivers exactly one INTERNAL reply after result settles; IpcServer drops only external canceled socket delivery. holdingForward in src/daemon/threads/maintenance-entry.ts resolves its held callback only when (reply delivered internally OR pre-admission canceled) AND request.lifetime.drained settles; keep hold through timed-out hanging preparation and through reaping. No early release on cancel or reply for work registered in lifetime. Router in src/daemon/threads/router.ts similarly calls once-only ended() after internal unary reply AND drained; no late socket write. For unrelated unary handlers with zero registered work drained resolves immediately at seal, preserving previous behavior. All relevant test methods remain main-daemon classified; on remote unary routes lacking a local lifetime use existing reply completion, do not serialize promises/functions. Ensure wrappers propagate the SAME lifetime object, including holdingForward's queued entry; if cancellation before forward admission, seal empty lifetime and release once. If synchronous handler throws, seal and internal reply; if supervisor preparation never settles, terminal client timeout still returned but slot/maintenance hold/activity remain truthfully held until drain; never fabricate cleanup. This intentionally prevents compaction/restart from racing unresolved store access and caps leaks to four admitted operations. Shutdown cancels operations, reaps children and waits registered drains; a still-unresolved noncancelable preparation is reported pending rather than releasing live resource ownership. Real-lock integration test: install production server/router/holdingForward with maintenance lock enabled, hold fake credential preparation deferred, reach real or injected deadline and receive timeout, attempt exclusive maintenance and assert denied while pending; repeat after socket disconnect and while child ignores cancel; settle preparation/reap then assert exclusive maintenance admitted and activity/holds/listeners zero exactly once.
